subject: general
question: Why were stupas built?
solution:
Correct answer is __**They contained sacred relics.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Buddhist stupas were initially built **to house the earthly remains of the historical Buddha and his associates** and are almost always established at sites sacred to Buddhism.
 
• The idea of a relic was later **increased to include sacred texts.**
 
• The stupa is an main form of **Buddhist architecture, **though it predates Buddhism. 
 
• It is usually examine to be a **sepulchral monument**—a place of burial or a receptacle for religious objects.
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00239362f124d988668536f6411bc7146c66603fdd940c4d4dd9573a57c1919a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Great Stupa, the most notable of the structures at the historic site of **Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh state, India**.​ 
 
• **The Great Stupa **was initially built in the** 3rd-century bce** by the **Mauryan emperor Ashoka.**
 
• The simple structure was damaged at some point through the **2nd-century bce.**
